focus: mcp-mobbin, mcp-refero, sk-code hub, sk-code-ci, sk-code-quality
noveltyJustification: All five findings are new because no prior lineage read these five packages; four establish no-candidate verdicts and one identifies the SD-003 answer-dependent companion.
keyQuestions: Which scenarios in the 28 unaudited packages meet Q2 or Q3 and should convert or gain a conversation companion, and which are blocked by the runner's five runtimes and three session actions?
Which existing single-prompt scenarios need updating rather than converting because the behavior is multi-turn but the current scenario checks it only once?
Which packages have no conversation candidate at all, so every scenario stays single prompt under Q1 or Q4?
Which multi-turn, answer-dependent, restart, compaction or cross-runtime behaviors in these packages lack any scenario that a conversation would add?
Which candidates rank highest by risk reduction relative to authoring and run cost across the 28 packages?
ruledOut: Treating a fresh Code Mode session as a runner restart

label: mcp-mobbin has no conversation candidate: its nine scenarios are read-only wiring, discovery, retrieval or refusal checks, each driven by one prompt or one doctor.sh command; the fresh Code Mode session precondition reloads an MCP server, not a runner session, so Q2 does not apply and Q4 keeps them single prompt.

mcp-refero has no conversation candidate: its nine scenarios are read-only wiring, discovery, funnel, quota or refusal checks, and the three-layer funnel runs inside one prompt; the Pro-account OAuth step is operator-only, so Q2 finds no answer-dependent turn and Q4 keeps them single prompt.

sk-code-ci has no conversation candidate: its eight scenarios are routing recall, routing-floor negatives, rule-reference fixtures and two doctor-script runs, each decided by a command transcript and exit status; Q2 finds no second exchange and Q4 keeps them single prompt.

sk-code-quality has no conversation candidate: its 23 scenarios each run the quality runner or a doctor script over a fixture and read a gate, exit code or check row; CQ-009's trust grant is a config key set between two runs, not a conversational answer, so Q2 does not apply and Q4 keeps them single prompt.

The sk-code hub has one add candidate: 22 of its 23 operator scenarios are one-prompt routing, load-set, restraint or hook checks (Q4), but SD-003 stops at the UNKNOWN disambiguation question and never exercises the answer-dependent turn that ROUTER.md section 6 requires, so a two-turn companion that answers runtime and verification commands would cover behavior no scenario checks (Q2).

direction: Treating a fresh Code Mode session as a runner restart
reason: The runner restarts the subject runtime, not the Code Mode MCP server, and no check observes the server reload.
Setting skilled.trustRepoChecks is an operator config action between two command runs, not a scripted conversational answer.
